condition: unstable maxillary complete denture causing a persistent painful palatal mucosal erosion over 3 weeks in an older adult
level_rationale: A 3-week history of a loose upper full denture rubbing a persistent painful raw mucosal erosion on the roof of the mouth in a 72-year-old adult requires dentist evaluation for prosthesis relining or adjustment and mucosal examination to exclude dysplasia, whereas the loose upper denture lodging stuck across the back of the throat constitutes an acute pharyngeal foreign-body airway emergency requiring immediate emergency department removal.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg, Abdulkader 2026) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + unsourced gum-shrinkage causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact pharyngeal denture impaction escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 72, 3 weeks of a loose upper full denture, and a painful raw sore rubbed on the roof of the mouth) without naming ulcer or using dialect words ('fit'/'fits'), with a 1-word span difference (21 vs 22 words), orthogonal 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing, zero stated negatives, and identical digit multisets across all 8 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rules A and D, escalating only f3 on the same loose upper denture from rubbing a palatal sore to lodging stuck across the back of the throat shifts care cleanly from dentist adjustment (level 3) to emergency department airway removal (level 4).
